problem: Decoupled RL agents using pretrained visual encoders (e.g., CLIP in EmbCLIP) are brittle to egocentric visual domain shifts (camera position, stride, illumination, etc.), and zero-shot adaptation to unseen domains is rarely addressed.
motivation: Embodied agents are deployed with uncalibrated physical and environmental factors that change their perception, so policies trained on source domains degrade in the target. The paper leverages prompt tuning of a frozen CLIP so that each prompt captures invariance to one domain factor, and combines them adaptively.
key_idea: Contrastively learn one visual prompt per domain factor on a frozen CLIP, then ensemble the prompted embeddings via a cosine-similarity-guided attention module trained jointly with the RL policy.
insight: Ensembling at the embedding level with guided attention beats uniform/weighted averaging and prompt-level combination (Unseen Target 79.7 vs 65.5 for the best alternative, ENS-UNI-AVG). Performance grows with the number of prompts up to about n=10 (unseen 43.0 at n=2 vs 79.7 at n=10) and then saturates. Attention weights are interpretable, peaking on the prompt matching the changed domain factor.
method: Prompt-based contrastive learning: for each domain factor, learn a visual prompt (length 8, in CLIP ViT-B/32 patch-embedding space) with an InfoNCE loss on positive pairs from ~10 expert episodes; the model is frozen and only the prompt is trained.

Contrast tasks: behavior-driven (same expert action), augmentation-driven (color perturbation for pixel-level factors like illumination), and timestep-driven (nearby timesteps across domains) positive pairs.
Guided-attention ensemble: compute z0=T(o) and prompted embeddings z_i=T(o,p_i); guidance g_i=cos(z0,z_i); weights are softmax(<z0,k_i>/sqrt(d) * g_i / tau); state Z=z0+sum w_i z_i.
Joint policy learning: the attention module (MLPs) and the policy are trained together with PPO (AI2THOR) or DAgger (Metaworld, CARLA) on 4 source domains, then deployed zero-shot.
Pretrained-policy adaptation: add a policy prompt p_pol for the frozen policy and update only the attention module (~400K samples, 10% of the policy-learning samples).
Semantic regularized augmentation: add Gaussian noise to prompted embeddings while a language prompt keeps object-level semantic predictions unchanged.

setting.backbone: CLIP ViT-B/32 (frozen) with learned visual prompts + attention MLPs + policy network (RL/IL trained)
setting.model_size: CLIP ViT-B/32 (~88M visual encoder); prompts and attention module are small
setting.training_data: ~10 expert episodes per domain factor for prompt learning (28,464 samples AI2THOR, 3,840 Metaworld, 7,394 CARLA); policy learned online with PPO in 4 source domains (3M steps) or DAgger
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (224x224) plus goal (object/point/image) and, for CARLA, sensor values
setting.action_space: AI2THOR discrete actions (MoveAhead, Rotate, Look, Done, etc.); Metaworld 4-D continuous end-effector; CARLA continuous steer/throttle/brake
setting.privileged: none at test; rule-based expert demonstrations are used for prompt learning

results: ConPE outperforms EmbCLIP, ATC, ACO, CURL and LUSR in zero-shot performance, e.g., AI2THOR ObjectNav unseen target 79.7 vs 59.0 for EmbCLIP (+20.7) and Metaworld Reach seen target 88.7 vs 71.3 for ATC. It also needs about 50–60% of EmbCLIP's samples to reach comparable success, and adapting a pretrained policy gives +3.5–7.0% in AI2THOR.
limitations: Only handles domain changes that fall within the predefined domain factors used for prompt learning.
Requires expert demonstrations for each domain factor, and evaluation is limited to simulation with a single AI2THOR scene (FloorPlan21) and synthetic domain shifts.
